query: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) is an α + β dual-phase alloy with low hardness and poor friction and wear properties under extreme-service and high-contact-stress conditions. Earlier studies explored redesigning the bulk alloy, which risks compromising its original advantages, and several surface-modification approaches. Traditional thermal spraying and thermal plating produced weak coatings with poor substrate bonding; composite coatings suffered from uneven constituent dispersion and weak interfaces; and laser cladding could generate intermetallic compounds, high residual stresses, cracks, and crazing. Prior refractory high-entropy-alloy studies reported improved hardness and wear resistance, but the broader requirements of compositional homogeneity, strong bonding, mechanical stability, and preservation of TC4’s beneficial properties remain. Formulate one neutral, testable hypothesis for an intervention that could satisfy these requirements. Specify the intervention, proposed mechanism, predicted outcome relative to untreated TC4, operating or test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Laser cladding a TiMoNbX (X = Ta, Cr, Zr) refractory high-entropy alloy coating on TC4 titanium alloy can improve its corrosion resistance and mechanical properties.
generation.intervention: Laser cladding of TiMoNbX (X = Ta, Cr, Zr) refractory high-entropy alloy coating
generation.conditions: 3.5% NaCl solution, potential scanning range from −1.2 V to 2.0 V, scanning speed 1 mV/s
generation.structural_mediator: BCC phase with β(Ti) structure, accompanied by a small amount of α’(Ti) with HCP structure
generation.mechanism: The rapid laser cladding process causes a fast cooling rate, resulting in a simple phase structure and preventing the formation of intermetallic compounds. The β-phase-stabilizing elements (Mo, V, Ta, Nb, Cr) contribute to the stability of the BCC phase.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved corrosion resistance and mechanical properties compared to untreated TC4 titanium alloy
generation.boundary: Operating conditions: 3.5% NaCl solution, potential scanning range from −1.2 V to 2.0 V, scanning speed 1 mV/s. Test boundaries: temperature range, scanning speed, and solution concentration.
generation.uncertainty: The effects of different refractory elements (Ta, Cr, Zr) on the corrosion resistance and mechanical properties of the TiMoNbX coating are not fully understood and require further investigation.

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled experiment with untreated TC4 titanium alloy and TiMoNbX (X = Ta, Cr, Zr) coated samples, tested in 3.5% NaCl solution with potential scanning range from −1.2 V to 2.0 V and scanning speed 1 mV/s.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the TiMoNbX coated samples show no significant improvement in corrosion resistance and mechanical properties compared to the untreated TC4 titanium alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.

Compared with other surface modification technologies, laser cladding technology has the advantages of fast cooling speed, small heat-affected zone, a wide selection of cladding materials, and economic and environmental protection, so it is more popular [,,,,]. By laser cladding a RHEA coating on the surface of titanium alloy, the advantages of the high strength and plasticity of the titanium alloy can be combined with the corrosion resistance of RHEA, which not only solves the defects of titanium alloy, but also greatly reduces the production cost and consumption in service.
At present, there is little research on the corrosion resistance of high-entropy alloys composed of refractory metal elements, but their excellent performance cannot be ignored. Jiang [] et al. prepared TiZrAlNb and TiZrAlNbCo high-entropy alloy coatings on the surface of TC4 titanium alloy using laser cladding technology. Although the passivation films formed by Ta, Cr and Zr have good corrosion resistance [,,,], no studies have compared the corrosion resistance of different elements Ta, Cr and Zr. We added Ta, Cr and Zr elements to a TiMoNb alloy to prepare the RHEA coating. The TiMoNb alloy phase has a BCC single-phase structure, which is conducive to the formation of RHEAs with a simple phase structure. By studying the corrosion resistance of the TiMoNbX (X = Ta, Cr, Zr) four-element RHEA after adding different refractory elements, we hope to deepen the understanding of the corrosion resistance mechanism of RHEA, and provide new theoretical data on and ways to improve the corrosion resistance of TC4 titanium alloy.

3.1. Microstructure and Phase Constitution of TiMoNbX (X = Ta, Cr, Zr) RHEA
Figure 1 shows the XRD pattern of the TiMoNbX (X = Cr, Ta, Zr) RHEA drawn using the Origin2019b software from the measured data. For convenience, the three TiMoNbCr, TiMoNbTa and TiMoNbZr RHEAs are respectively denoted as +Cr, +Ta and +Zr.
It can be observed from Figure 1 that there is one strong peak and four weak peaks in similar positions in the XRD patterns of the RHEA coatings with +Cr, +Ta and +Zr. The strong peaks appeared at 39.2°, while the weak peaks appeared at 36.8°, 40.5°, 56.1° and 70.9°, respectively. It should be noted that there is an additional weak peak at 84.4° in the XRD pattern of the +Ta coating, while the weak peak appears at 77.0° in the XRD pattern of the +Zr coating.
